name: Opus EDM
description: Enterprise data management for instrument, party and pricing reference data: vendor feeds are ingested, reconciled into a golden copy, and the rule breaches that reconciliation raises are worked as exceptions by a data steward.
notes: This registration is real, not illustrative. Every domain listed under `metadata.domains` is a domain the demo tenant's catalog actually contains, scanned from a live MS SQL Server through @opus/catalog-ingest; every `definitionRef` is a page that ships in apps/viewer/public/definitions. What is NOT here is as deliberate: no components, because every component in the library today is platform-native and claiming one for EDM would misrepresent who maintains it; no `metadata.dataSources`, because a source id is assigned per tenant when a steward registers the database and hard-coding this tenant's would be wrong everywhere else.

glossary.definition: The single approved value for an attribute after every vendor's value for it has been reconciled under the active rule set. It is a derived value with a recorded provenance, not one vendor's value promoted.
One vendor's value for one attribute of one security, as delivered, before reconciliation. Retained after reconciliation so a golden copy can always be traced back to what each vendor said.
A steward's deliberate substitution of a value the rules chose, recorded with who, when and why. An override is a governed decision, not a correction of a mistake.
A rule breach raised during validation or reconciliation that a person has to clear. Carries a severity, an age, and an assignee.
A data quality or reconciliation test evaluated on ingestion. A rule that fires produces an exception; the rule is the standard, the exception is the instance.
One delivery of one vendor file through ingestion, with its own step-by-step processing history and outcome.
A party that can be a counterparty, issuer or account holder, positioned in an ownership hierarchy.

templates.name: Security Master Dashboard
templates.intent: A morning health check over the security master: how many securities, how much moved, what needs attention. The starting point for a dashboard about reference data completeness rather than about processing.

templates.name: Operations Dashboard
templates.intent: Today's processing: files in, files late, files failed, and the exceptions they raised. The starting point for an operational shift-handover view.

systemJourneys.name: Security investigation
systemJourneys.description: The path a steward walks when a figure on the master dashboard looks wrong: find the security, read its golden copy and per-vendor source values, check who is related to it, then work whatever exceptions it raised. This is the journey the shipped `securities.operations` experience already wires by drill-down; registering it names the path so it can be navigated deliberately rather than discovered.

systemJourneys.name: Processing triage
systemJourneys.description: The operational path: something is late or failed, so open the load, read its steps, and clear the exceptions it produced.

actions.label: Assign exception
actions.description: Give an open exception an owner. The one action the Exception Queue's unassigned count exists to prompt.

actions.label: Clear exception
actions.description: Close an exception, recording the resolution. Closing is a decision about data, so it is capability-gated rather than available to anyone who can see the queue.

actions.label: Propose override
actions.description: Substitute a value the rules chose, for approval. Proposing and approving are separate capabilities on purpose — an override nobody else saw is an undocumented change to the golden copy.

actions.label: Reprocess file load
actions.description: Re-run a failed or partial load. Mutating, because a second run replaces what the first produced.

actions.label: View lineage
actions.description: Trace a golden copy value back through reconciliation to each vendor's source value. Read-only, and the answer to nearly every question that starts "why does it say that".

capabilities.label: Read processing
capabilities.description: File loads and their step history.

capabilities.label: Read securities
capabilities.description: The security master and its per-vendor source values.

capabilities.label: Read parties
capabilities.description: Legal entities, customer accounts and their hierarchies.

capabilities.label: Read data quality
capabilities.description: Rules and the exceptions they raise.

capabilities.label: Read exception assignees
capabilities.description: Who owns an exception. Separate from reading the exception itself, because who is working what is personnel information in some deployments.

capabilities.label: Approve overrides
capabilities.description: Held separately from proposing, so the same person cannot do both.

capabilities.label: See data quality surfaces
capabilities.description: Whether the Studio shows this user data quality widgets at all. Distinct from `edm.dq.read`, which decides whether the rows come back — one is what the product offers, the other is what the data permits.

roles.label: Data Steward
roles.description: Owns the golden copy. Works exceptions and proposes overrides; does not approve their own.

roles.label: Data Owner
roles.description: Accountable for a data domain. Approves what a steward proposes.

roles.label: Operations
roles.description: Runs ingestion. Sees processing and the exceptions it raised, not the party master.

roles.label: Data Consumer
roles.description: Reads reference data. No remediation authority of any kind.

terminology.means: A tradable financial instrument in the master — an equity, bond or fund with identifiers, pricing and issuer relationships.
terminology.notToBeConfusedWith: Information security. In this product 'security' almost never means access control, and a request to 'add security data' is asking for instruments.

terminology.means: A legal entity, counterparty, issuer or account holder in the party master.
terminology.notToBeConfusedWith: A person, or a party to a transaction in the legal sense. A party here is a mastered record with a hierarchy position.

terminology.means: A rule breach raised during validation or reconciliation that somebody has to clear, carrying a severity, an age and an assignee.
terminology.notToBeConfusedWith: A software error or a thrown exception. An EDM exception is a unit of work, and 'how many exceptions' asks about a queue, not about failures.

terminology.means: A steward's recorded substitution of a value the reconciliation rules chose.
terminology.notToBeConfusedWith: A correction or a fix. An override does not mean the rules were wrong — it means a person's judgement takes precedence in this instance, and the rule's result is retained alongside it.

terminology.means: The single approved value for an attribute after reconciling every vendor's value for it.
terminology.notToBeConfusedWith: A backup, an archive, or a snapshot. It is the current authoritative value, not a copy kept aside.

terminology.means: One vendor's value for an attribute before reconciliation, retained for lineage.
One delivery of one vendor file through ingestion, with a step history and an outcome.
terminology.notToBeConfusedWith: Loading a page. 'Late loads' is about vendor files arriving after their expected time.

terminology.means: A data quality or reconciliation test evaluated on ingestion; when it fires it raises an exception.
terminology.notToBeConfusedWith: A business rule in a workflow. A rule here is a test over data, not a branch in a process.

terminology.means: A reference data supplier whose feeds are ingested and reconciled.
terminology.notToBeConfusedWith: A software supplier. Vendors here are data sources with feeds, timeliness expectations and quality histories.

terminology.means: The count of things a steward is expected to act on now — open exceptions plus late or failed loads. A composite figure, not a single table's row count.

instructions: Prefer 'golden copy' over 'master value' and 'exception' over 'error' — these are the words the product's users use, and a page labelled in generic terms reads as though it belongs to a different system.
A count of exceptions is nearly always wanted as open-and-unresolved, not all-time. Say which you used.
Ageing matters more than volume in this domain: an exception open for two weeks is a worse fact than fifty raised this morning. When a queue is on a page, put its ageing next to its count.
Never propose a page that shows an assignee without checking `edm.dq.assignee.read` — who is working what is personnel information in some deployments.

hints.whenToUse: Any request about instrument or party reference data, vendor feed processing, data quality exceptions, overrides, or lineage back to a vendor's value.
exampleQuestions: Create a Security Master Operations Dashboard showing today's files processed, late files, failed files, exceptions, new securities, and data quality KPIs
Show me the oldest unassigned data quality exceptions by severity
Which vendor feeds were late this week and what did they break
